title: A 5760 by 3840 file on XAVC HS 4K and XAVC S 4K at 23.98p and 25p: encoder request, two encoder cores, the 4K memory blocks in an order that holds the picture, descriptors, profiles and the monitoring label; every record setting with I and P pictures only (M = 1), and the MP4 edit list starting at 0; the MP4 headers (tkhd, stsd, PROF) say 5760x3840
goes_with: dmmwb4688_c2_v1 + og57n_c2_v1 (the real 5760x3840 picture) and og57cp_c2_v3, all in coprocessor RAM
level: Level 6 (HEVC 180, AVC 60); Level 6.1 (183, 61) in the 300 Mbps profiles
encoder_cores: both (UseCore 2), as every stock descriptor above 249 million pixels a second
while_applied: the formats' other frame rates find no descriptor: their recordings are refused at encoder open
the container and the metadata still say 3840 by 2160

the 100M record settings (and any higher one of these formats) record at 300 Mbps; the lower settings keep their bit rate; the menu, the remaining-time figure and the container's own bit-rate fields still say what the setting says
every record setting of XAVC HS 4K and XAVC S 4K at 23.98p and 25p records with M = 1: I and P pictures only, no B pictures, no picture reordering

an HEVC MP4 recorded normally has a video edit list starting at 0 (libmpr.so 0x11f4e0); right for M = 1 HEVC. AVC keeps its one-frame start, which its constant one-frame composition offset needs (C0557). An HEVC stream with B pictures would show its first picture one frame late
the MP4 headers of XAVC HS 4K and XAVC S 4K files say 5760x3840 (3:2); Sony's XML in the file still says 3840x2160, 16:9

writer set-up 0x11f030 (a normal recording): the video edit list's start in frames, MP4 request +0x10 (0x222b18 -> libXavcMp4 +0x50 -> 0x226818: media_time = frame duration x it). HEVC branch: `csel w0, w1, w0, ls` (2 frames at 50p and up, else 1) -> `mov w0, #0`. AVC (0x11fe60: 1 frame), intra formats and the [x21+4] path unchanged. With M = 1 an HEVC stream has no composition offsets, so a one-frame start hides its first picture (F981, F986)
clip-format row 1 (8192x4320, code 3; unused on this camera) -> 5760x3840, code 23, the code row 5 gives a 3840x2160 recording. Row 5 is left as it is
MP4 track height, XAVC S 4K (AVC, combs 0, 2): 2160 -> 3840 (`mov w6, #0x870` -> `mov`)
MP4 track width, XAVC S 4K (AVC, combs 0, 2): 3840 -> 5760 (`mov w7, #0xf00` -> `mov`)
MP4 track height, XAVC HS 4K (HEVC, combs 5, 7): 2160 -> 3840 (`mov w6, #0x870` -> `mov`)
MP4 track width, XAVC HS 4K (HEVC, combs 5, 7): 3840 -> 5760 (`mov w7, #0xf00` -> `mov`)
stsd entry set-up 0x2240cc: its 7680 compare -> 5760, so a 5760-wide entry is built (else it returns 2) (`mov w1, #0x1e00` -> `mov`)
PROF profile id 0x2256fc, AVC: width read -> the constant 3840 (the UHD ids) (`ldrh w3, [x1, #0x2a]` -> `mov`)
PROF profile id 0x2256fc, HEVC chroma code 2: width read -> the constant 3840 (`ldrh w0, [x1, #0x2a]` -> `mov`)
PROF profile id 0x2256fc, HEVC chroma code 1: width read -> the constant 3840 (`ldrh w0, [x1, #0x2a]` -> `mov`)
PROF pixel aspect 0x225d30: its 7680 compare -> 5760 (1:1), else it returns 3 (`mov w0, #0x1e00` -> `mov`)
